statement: The cited all-finite centralizer proofs contain an unverified closure-intersection step. A noncircular induction from prime-power normalizer and congruence inputs proves the solvable comparison. For geometric A5 on a punctured sphere, the completed and discrete centralizers have the same puncture-permutation image: exceptional orbits are fixed pointwise and m free orbits have image A5^m semidirect S_m. The pure completion equality at all refinements remains unproved here.
depends_on: R-Boggi, prime-power case of Theorem A and Corollary B
manuscript_passages: Part D(b) and Part F(b): nonsolvable completion centralizers
notes: No counterexample to the source theorem is asserted. The two maps from completed discrete centralizer to its closure and from that closure to the ambient completed centralizer are typed separately. The exact remaining finite-refinement intersection criterion is proved by compactness. For the minimal twelve-puncture action, the residual centralizer is placed inside the specified embedded Fhat13 pure A4 centralizer and all24 six-point plus all12 seven-point forgetting kernels. The six-point joint map is proved noninjective by two explicit invisible peripheral meridians. The seven-point maps retain all14 collision points; their executed joint H1 map over F101 has rank6 and kernel dimension7. F.9 subsequently proves the full seven-point map noninjective; the actual centralizer remains undetermined. All finite tests are executed. F8 now proves equality of all twelve seven-point kernels, absence of nonidentity reducible elements in the discrete kernel, and trivial intersection of the completed kernel with every conjugate of every full source cusp. Each cusp is detected by a four-point twist character with multiplier one or two. F.9 gives an explicit nontrivial common kernel word, with embedded full procyclic closure, and proves that every six-point constraint factors through a seven-point one. The A5 centralizer equality remains unproved.
